short: Send page context to your webhooks with reusable templates and smart rules. A product of hexly.ai.
headline: Your page. In motion.
summary: Turn the page you are on into a useful next step. Send its URL, title, selected text, and metadata to the webhooks you choose.
description:
Hooky — Your page. In motion.

Keep the useful parts of a page moving. Send a link to your reading list, share a selection with your own automation, or trigger a workflow without leaving Chrome. You choose the webhook. Hooky brings the page context.

WHAT'S NEW IN 2.0

A compact purple workspace puts templates, request previews, and page variables within easy reach. See the current page in the popup, edit resolved values before sending, and try a sample URL or title before saving a Quick Send rule. Fine borders, quiet shadows, and light, dark, or system themes keep the interface clear.

MAKE A TEMPLATE. USE IT AGAIN.

Save independent templates with a name, endpoint URL, HTTP method, and key-value parameters. Switch templates from the popup or settings. Choose GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE. GET and DELETE use query parameters; POST, PUT, and PATCH send a JSON object with string values. A request preview shows how the configured request is assembled.

BRING THE PAGE WITH YOU

Use any of these variables in parameter values:

• {{page.url}} — page URL
• {{page.title}} — page title
• {{page.selection}} — selected text
• {{page.meta.description}} — description metadata
• {{page.meta.og:title}} — Open Graph title
• {{page.meta.og:description}} — Open Graph description
• {{page.meta.og:image}} — Open Graph image URL

Click a variable in settings to insert it into a parameter. Combine variables with your own text, including multiline notes. Missing values become empty strings. The popup shows the resolved values and lets you edit them before sending.

ONE CLICK WHEN THE PAGE MATCHES

Quick Send rules choose a template when you click the toolbar icon. Match the page URL or title using contains, equals, starts with, ends with, or a regular expression. Matching ignores case. Enable or disable rules, test a sample, and move rules up or down in priority.

The first enabled matching rule with a valid template sends immediately. If no applicable rule is found, Hooky opens the popup. Rules run on your toolbar click, not automatically as you browse.

RIGHT-CLICK TO SEND

Your templates also appear in the Hooky context menu. Choose one to send with the page's available context. A brief toolbar badge shows success or failure. The popup provides request status after sending.

SMALL BY DESIGN

Hooky uses native JavaScript and local assets, with no UI framework, analytics, account, or publisher relay. Templates, rules, and preferences stay in your browser's local storage. Page context is read on demand; requests go to the endpoint you configured. That receiving service controls what happens to the data afterward.

SET UP IN A MINUTE

1. Open Hooky Settings and create a webhook template.
2. Enter your receiving endpoint, method, and parameters.
3. Add page variables if needed, then save.
4. Open a webpage, choose the template, review the values, and send.

You provide a compatible webhook or automation endpoint. Hooky does not provide built-in service accounts, custom HTTP headers, or full-page text extraction.

Available in English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, German, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, and Russian. The interface follows Chrome's language. Requires Chrome 127 or later.

release:
Hooky 2.0.0

• New compact purple popup and settings workspace, with the original Hooky logo.
• Current-page context, editable popup values, request preview, and click-to-insert variables.
• Multiline parameter editing, rule sample testing, and priority controls.
• Light, dark, and system themes; updated interface strings in all 10 languages.
• Literal values edited in the popup are sent exactly once without re-resolving variable syntax.
• Existing templates, rules, and settings are retained. Native JavaScript runtime and local assets.
• Requires Chrome 127 or later. No new permissions.

purpose: Send user-configured webhook requests with context from the active browser page, using reusable templates and optional click-triggered matching rules.
permissions:
activeTab
Reads the active page URL and title after a user gesture, and authorizes on-demand access to selection and metadata. Used by the toolbar popup, Quick Send action, and context menu.

scripting
Runs the small page-context extraction function in the active tab when needed. No persistent content script runs on page navigation.

storage
Stores webhook templates, active-template selection, Quick Send rules, and theme preferences locally using chrome.storage.local. No cloud sync.

contextMenus
Lists the user's configured templates in the Hooky right-click menu so they can trigger a webhook from the current page.

Host permissions: <all_urls>
Allows cross-origin HTTP/HTTPS requests to arbitrary webhook endpoints explicitly configured by the user, including endpoints without browser CORS support. Endpoint domains cannot be known at installation. The extension does not crawl tabs or send browsing activity to the publisher.
data:
Publisher collection: none. No analytics, advertising, account, request relay, or remote executable code.
Local storage: template names, destination URLs, parameter values, rules, and theme. User-entered parameters may contain credentials or personal information.
Website content: page URL/title, current selection, description metadata, and selected Open Graph fields are read on demand. Configured variables determine what is sent.
Browsing data: no ongoing navigation history is recorded; the active page URL/title may be transmitted in a triggered request.
Destinations: user-configured endpoints, subject to browser redirect handling. Receiving services can see normal network metadata such as IP address.
Purpose: perform the webhook action chosen by the user. No sale, advertising use, or credit/lending use of data.
Deletion: remove templates/rules or uninstall for local data; previously delivered data must be managed at the receiving endpoint.
